To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose an algorithm that can effectively select training data for speeding up support vector machines.
we propose an efficient algorithm for concept boundary detection, which can be used to select boundary training instances for speeding up SVM training.

(a) SVMs can be effectively accelerated by using our proposed concept boundary detection technique, which is based on a novel preprocessing step that prepares nearest-neighbor lists, (b) the preprocessing step is concept-independent, i.e., the same preprocessing step can be used for any concept, and (c) our technique can be applied to both linear and non-linear SVMs, and can be used to accelerate SVM training in any domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Given n training instances, how to select the minimum number of training data for SVMs to achieve high classification accuracy?
the following questions.
the following two problems: (1) How can we reduce the number of training data without compromising testing accuracy? (2) How can we speed up the training phase of SVMs?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed concept boundary detection algorithm can effectively speed up SVM training without significantly compromising testing results, especially for high-dimensional data.
the proposed concept boundary detection algorithm is effective in speeding up SVMs without significantly compromising their testing accuracy, outperforming the other downsampling algorithms.
our algorithm reduces the training time by 10 to 100 times while maintaining the same testing accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our algorithm can speed up training of SVMs by reducing the training data size, while keeping the testing accuracy at the same level.
we have proposed an algorithm to reduce the training set size for SVMs, which is effective and efficient, while preserving high classification accuracy.
, by combining the proposed algorithm with the existing downsampling algorithms, we can achieve the same testing accuracy with less training time and less training data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the O(n2) SVM training cost is not a fundamental barrier to scalability, and can be reduced to an extent that makes SVMs practical for large data sets.
, in the context of SVMs, concept boundary detection can be a powerful technique for speeding up training.

, in order to reduce training time of SVMs, we should focus on reducing the number of training examples rather than reducing the number of features, as is often done in other machine learning algorithms.
